text: If you're comparing like Zen 5 to Arrow Lake CPUs for example, Arrow Lake is usually able to handle higher memory clocks and will get more out of kits with relatively higher speeds and looser timings. Also, if you're getting an X3D CPU, your ram choice is going to impact your performance less than it would on CPUs with relatively less cache. That being said, I don't really think either of those are considerations that complicate things all that much. First of all, the differences we're talking about are relatively minor, and once you get to optimizing your kits that much, you're probably doing your own tweaks to expo profiles and I think at that point you have a pretty good idea what to look for. Usually most people are just gonna pick what CPU to get, and decide on a motherboard or RAM from there, and that's probably the right way to go about it 99% of the time.
